module

public import Mathlib.NumberTheory.NumberField.Basic
public import FormalConjecturesForMathlib.Algebra.QuadraticAlgebra.Instances

public section

open Algebra (IsQuadraticExtension)
open Module NumberField

/-- Any `QuadraticAlgebra ℚ a b` that is a field is automatically a quadratic extension
of `ℚ`, i.e., a degree-2 extension. Combined with `IsQuadraticField.instNumberField`,
this gives `NumberField (QuadraticAlgebra ℚ a b)` for free. -/
instance QuadraticAlgebra.instIsQuadraticExtension (a b : ℚ) [Fact (∀ r : ℚ, r ^ 2 ≠ a + b * r)] :
    IsQuadraticExtension ℚ (QuadraticAlgebra ℚ a b) where
  finrank_eq_two' := QuadraticAlgebra.finrank_eq_two a b

/-- A quadratic field is a number field: it has characteristic zero
and is finite-dimensional over `ℚ`. -/
instance Algebra.IsQuadraticExtension.to_numberField (K : Type*) [Field K] [CharZero K]
    [IsQuadraticExtension ℚ K] : NumberField K where
  to_finiteDimensional := .of_finrank_pos <| by grind [IsQuadraticExtension.finrank_eq_two]

findings.description: In the use-site file FormalConjectures/Wikipedia/WallSunSun.lean, lines 147–149, the predicate `{p | ∃ a b, a ^ 2 - 4 * b = D ∧ IsLucasWieferichPrime a b p}` does not express the field-based Wall–Sun–Sun property. The Lucas parameters may depend on p. For D = 5 it already admits p = 3: choose a = 9, b = 19; the relevant index is 4 and U₄(9,19) = 387 is divisible by 9, although 3 is not a Wall–Sun–Sun prime (L₃ = 4). Both facts were proved in Lean. More generally, for every admissible D and every odd prime p not dividing D, choose a divisible by p² with a² ≡ D mod 4, and put b = (a²-D)/4. The index p−(D/p) is even, and a divides every even-indexed U_n(a,b), so the predicate holds automatically. The claimed infinitude is therefore elementary, not the cited conjecture. The quadratic-field instances themselves are correct; the error is identifying an arbitrary Lucas presentation with the prescribed unit of that field.
findings.source_evidence: Wikipedia, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wall%E2%80%93Sun%E2%80%93Sun_prime, section “Wall–Sun–Sun primes with discriminant D”, says that D = 5 gives the conventional Wall–Sun–Sun primes and conjectures infinitude for each non-one fundamental discriminant. Its cited primary source, Elsenhans–Jahnel, “The Fibonacci sequence modulo p² — An investigation by computer for p < 10¹⁴”, arXiv:1006.0824, §2.2, remark beginning “One might want to put the concept of an exceptional prime into the wider context of algebraic number theory”, defines the real-quadratic-field property using a fundamental unit ε and congruences in O_K/(p²), not an arbitrary pair of Lucas coefficients.
findings.suggested_fix: Define the prime predicate from the quadratic number field of field discriminant D and the prescribed unit data, rather than existentially choosing Lucas coefficients after p. In the real-quadratic case, use a fundamental unit ε and the source's congruences ε^(p−1) ≡ 1 mod p² in the split case and ε^(2p+2) ≡ 1 mod p² in the inert case. Ensure that the D = 5 specialization recovers the conventional Wall–Sun–Sun predicate. Merely fixing the polynomial discriminant, or adding irreducibility, does not supply the fundamental-unit condition.

findings.description: The docstring cites `IsQuadraticField.instNumberField`, which does not exist in this checkout. The instance that supplies the promised NumberField structure is `Algebra.IsQuadraticExtension.to_numberField`. This is only a stale reference: the mathematical claim and automatic instance synthesis are correct.
findings.source_evidence: FormalConjecturesForMathlib/NumberTheory/NumberField/Quadratic.lean, lines 26–37: the first docstring names `IsQuadraticField.instNumberField`, whereas the second declaration is `Algebra.IsQuadraticExtension.to_numberField`. Searches of the repository and Mathlib found no declaration with the referenced name; Lean successfully synthesized the promised NumberField instance.

reformulations.difference: Instead of assuming explicitly that the canonical quadratic algebra is a field, the instance assumes `Fact (∀ r : ℚ, r ^ 2 ≠ a + b * r)`.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: The canonical algebra is ℚ[X]/(X²−bX−a), so the hypothesis is precisely the absence of a rational root of its defining quadratic. In /workspace/review/scratch.lean I proved `(∀ r : ℚ, r ^ 2 ≠ a + b * r) ↔ IsField (QuadraticAlgebra ℚ a b)`. The forward implication uses Mathlib's field instance. Conversely, a root r gives two nonzero elements ω−r and ω−(b−r) whose product is zero. Its basis has two elements, so the resulting field has degree exactly two. The hypothesis therefore excludes exactly the non-field cases, not any intended quadratic fields.

review.notes: Both instances in the reviewed module are mathematically faithful. I checked their elaborated types, canonical ℚ-algebra structures, finite-rank conventions, and use-site hypotheses. Tests cover ℚ(i), ℚ(√2), the split and dual-number cases, exclusion of ℚ itself, and squarefree radicands 0 and 1. The source still records the conventional existence and infinitude questions as open; the downstream finding is a mathematical mismatch, not stale status. The explicit exclusion of discriminant 1 in the library predicate does not change the cited non-one-discriminant conjecture. Successful scratch files are /workspace/review/scratch.lean, use_sites.lean, discriminant_variant.lean, and discriminant_every_prime.lean. The last file proves the entire formalized infinitude assertion at D = 5 using elementary Lucas divisibility and Euclid's theorem. The equivalence and counterexample/infinitude proofs have no sorryAx dependency. No repository source files were changed.
